_comment: Ground truth by construction: each entry is keyed by the exact GET URL fired by one, and only one, fixture code path (see eval/provenance_benchmark/extension/*.js). true_origin is the human-known TRUE cause of the request; expected_prediction is what Section 5.1's documented, already-known behaviour of the current attributor (sandbox/sensors/cdp_sw.py + worker/risk.py:317-359) predicts BEFORE running - the benchmark's job is to measure whether that prediction actually holds, not to assume it.

https://gt-page.bench/gt/page_js.expected_rationale: Page's own inline <script>, no extension code involved at all - baseline negative control.

https://gt-cscript.bench/gt/content_scri.expected_rationale: Isolated-world content-script fetch, synchronous top-level call - the case _initiator_is_extension is designed to catch.

https://gt-sw.bench/gt/service_worker.expected_rationale: origin==service_worker is trusted unconditionally by worker/risk.py, bypassing the initiator-stack check entirely.

https://gt-injected.bench/gt/injected_sc.expected_rationale: Known limitation (Section 5.1): content_scripts world:MAIN executes as the page's own JS realm, http(s) URL not chrome-extension://, so the initiator stack shows no extension frame - expected miss. (Manual DOM script injection was tried first and found CSP-blocked by Chrome itself, independent of ExtAnalyze - see cs_inject.js comment.)

https://gt-async.bench/gt/async_callback.expected_rationale: Known limitation (Section 5.1): the fetch fires across a setTimeout macrotask boundary from content-script code - expected miss if CDP's initiator.stack does not chain across the async boundary; NOT guaranteed, this is exactly what we measure.
